company.name: Indus Insurance
company.mission: We help families face the worst days of life with dignity. We give honest advice, fair products, and we pay claims without a fight.

glossary.def: The money a policyholder pays, every month or every year, to keep a policy active.
Pure protection for a fixed number of years. It pays only if the sad event happens inside those years.
Protection for the full life of the insured person. It usually has a savings part too.
Know Your Customer. We check the identity documents of a client before we issue a policy.
Anti Money Laundering checks. They stop people from hiding illegal money in insurance.
First Notification of Loss. It is the first report a client makes when something goes wrong. Every claim starts here.
Treatment where the patient stays in hospital. Most health plans start their cover here.
Motor cover with accidents, theft and third party liability. It is not only damage to others.

stations.name: Lobby and Reception
stations.objective: Know the company. Its mission, its story, and who does what.

intro.speaker: Ms. Rahman
intro.text: Welcome. Every Indus story starts in this lobby. Our story too. Before anything else, you should know the company you are now a part of.

intro.speaker: Ms. Rahman
intro.text: On the wall behind me is our journey. It has five milestones, and right now they are in the wrong order. It is a small first day tradition here. Put them in the right order, and the Company Insider badge is yours.

intro.speaker: Ms. Rahman
intro.text: One hint from someone who has watched it all happen: we looked after people's health for years before we insured their cars. At Indus, health came first.

stations.missionIntro: Tap the milestones in the order they happened. Start with the earliest one.

timeline.text: Indus starts in Lahore. The first policy is sold and framed. It still hangs in this lobby.
The health line starts. The first hospital cash cover plan of Indus reaches 10,000 families.
The motor desk opens. Our claims promise is written. A decision in 10 working days.
The CRM time begins. Every policy journey moves to one system, from lead to renewal.
Indus crosses 500,000 active policyholders in Pakistan.

stations.wrongFeedback: Not quite. Think. What had to exist before this could happen? Try again.
stations.success: That is our story, in the right order. Clients ask about it again and again. Now you can answer them.

stations.name: Product Hall. Life Desk
stations.objective: Learn the difference between term life and whole life, and match every client to the right one.

intro.speaker: Bilal
intro.text: Welcome to the Life Desk. Rule one here. We never sell a product. We match a need. Two products live on this desk. Term Life gives pure protection for a set number of years. The premium is low, and there is no payout if the term ends safely. Whole Life gives protection for full life, with a savings part, so it costs more.

intro.speaker: Bilal
intro.text: Four clients are waiting for you. For every client, pick the product that fits. Then tell me why. If your reason is right, you have understood the product.

stations.missionIntro: For every client, pick the right product first. Then pick the right reason.

productFeedback.wrongTerm: Think again about the need of this client. Does the need end on a date, or does it last a lifetime?
productFeedback.wrongWhole: Think again about the need of this client. Does the need end on a date, or does it last a lifetime?

clients.name: Ahmed, 29. Newly married. Home loan of Rs. 8 million
clients.need: If something happens to him, the loan and the income of his family must stay safe. He needs maximum cover with minimum premium.

reasons.text: Term life gives the biggest cover for the lowest premium, for the same years as the loan.
Whole life builds savings, so it must be safer for his family.
reasons.feedback: Savings sound safe, but they make the cover small, and his family needs big cover. When the need is pure protection on a small budget, term wins.

clients.name: Mrs. Qureshi, 52. She wants to leave something behind for her grandchildren
clients.need: She is not protecting an income. She wants a sure legacy, and it must last her whole life.

reasons.text: Whole life stays active for life, so the legacy is there when it is needed.
Term life is cheaper, so she can buy more of it.
reasons.feedback: Cheaper, yes. But a term can end while she is still alive, and then the legacy is gone. Her need has no end date.

clients.name: Danish, 34. Only earner at home. Two small children. Tight monthly budget
clients.need: If he is gone, his family must live on the payout for many years. Every rupee of premium counts.

reasons.text: Term life gives the biggest payout for every rupee of premium in the years when the children need him most.
Whole life, because children need cover for their whole life.
reasons.feedback: The children need cover while they depend on his income, about 15 to 20 years. A lifelong product costs many times more, for cover they do not need at that age.

clients.name: Mr. Sheikh, 60. Retired. He wants funeral costs and final expenses covered
clients.need: A small cover that never ends, so his family never has to arrange money in a hard week.

reasons.text: Whole life gives a sure payout whenever it happens. This is exactly what final expense cover is for.
Term life for 5 years at a time is enough.
reasons.feedback: At his age, a new term can be refused, or it can end before it is needed. Final expenses have no last date, so the cover must have no last date too.

stations.success: Four clients, four honest matches. That is the whole job at this desk. The product serves the need. The need never serves the product.

stations.name: Product Hall. Health and Motor Desks
stations.objective: Tell clearly what the Health and Motor policies cover, and what they do not cover.

intro.speaker: Sana
intro.text: This is the health desk. The fastest way to lose the trust of a client is simple. Let them believe something is covered when it is not. So we learn the edges of the policy, not only the middle.

intro.speaker: Omar
intro.text: And this is the motor desk. The same rule, on wheels. Six real situations are coming. For every one, you will decide. Covered, or not covered? There is no penalty for a wrong guess. But I will explain every answer, because one day a client will ask you the same question.

stations.missionIntro: Six scenarios. Decide with honesty. The client deserves the true answer, not the easy one.

scenarios.text: Health: A policyholder stays in hospital for one night for dengue fever. He needs a private room.
scenarios.why: Hospital stay for illness is the heart of the health policy. The room and the treatment are covered.

scenarios.text: Health: A policyholder wants the policy to pay for cosmetic surgery to remove a scar.
scenarios.why: Cosmetic work is not included. The policy pays for medical need, not for looks.

scenarios.text: Health: A policyholder visits a clinic for a routine check up and blood tests, then goes home.
scenarios.why: Clinic visits and routine tests are not in this plan. Cover starts when the patient is admitted to hospital. This is a classic mix up. Sana writes it on the whiteboard every Monday.

scenarios.text: Motor: The car of a policyholder is damaged in a crash with another vehicle on the motorway.
scenarios.why: Damage from a crash is exactly what comprehensive motor cover is for.

scenarios.text: Motor: The engine of a policyholder becomes old and weak. The car needs a full engine repair.
scenarios.why: Old age damage and engine failure with time are not included. Insurance covers sudden accidents, not slow ageing.

scenarios.text: Motor: The parked car of a policyholder is stolen at night. It is never found.
scenarios.why: Theft is a main covered event in comprehensive motor cover. First the police report, the FIR, is filed. Then the claim process starts.

stations.success: Now you know the edges of both policies. Clients remember the advisor who told them the truth before the claim, not after it.

stations.name: Compliance and Legal Zone
stations.objective: Do the basics of KYC and AML, and spot red flags.

intro.speaker: Farah
intro.text: Welcome to Compliance. This department keeps Indus honest. My rule is simple. No policy leaves this building on incomplete papers. And we never promise a client something the policy does not say.

intro.speaker: Farah
intro.text: Three applications came to my desk this morning. Every file has exactly ONE red flag. It can be a missing document, a detail that does not match, or a promise that must never be made. Find the flag in every file. The other details are fine. Please do not invent problems.

stations.missionIntro: Read every application with care. Tap the ONE detail that is a red flag.

applications.client: Application 1 of 3. Mr. Tariq Mehmood. Term Life

details.text: CNIC copy is attached and clear to read
Date of birth on the form matches the CNIC
Nominee is written: the wife of the applicant, with her CNIC number
Medical declaration is blank. The applicant wrote: will fill later
details.why: A policy cannot be issued on an incomplete declaration. This word, later, is where claim disputes are born. The complete form comes back, or the application waits.

applications.client: Application 2 of 3. Ms. Areeba Shah. Health

details.text: Form is signed by the applicant
CNIC number on the form ends with 4213. The CNIC copy ends with 4231
details.why: Two digits do not match. It may be a small typing mistake, but KYC means we check, we do not guess. The application goes back for correction before anything is issued.

details.text: Premium payment is received in full

applications.client: Application 3 of 3. Mr. Joseph D'Souza. Whole Life

details.text: Age of the applicant is checked with the CNIC
Note of the advisor: I assured the client that this plan gives 12 percent returns every year, guaranteed
details.why: This promise must never be made. Savings growth is a projection. It is never a guarantee. The note is removed, the advisor is coached, and the client is told the true position before he signs.

stations.wrongFeedback: That detail is fine. Every application here has exactly one real flag. Look again. Is something missing? Does something not match? Was something promised that should never be promised?
stations.success: Three files, three flags. And you left the good details alone. This judgement is the whole job here. Catch what is wrong. Do not block what is right.

stations.name: Claims Hall
stations.objective: Learn the claim journey. FNOL, assessment, decision.

intro.speaker: Daniyal
intro.text: This is Claims Hall. The promise of Indus is tested here. A client calls us on one of the worst days of their year. Our promise is clear. A decision in 10 working days. That promise works only if the journey runs in the right order.

intro.speaker: Daniyal
intro.text: First, put the claim journey in order. It has five steps, from the first call of the client to the money in their account. After that, I will give you two live situations. You will judge them.

stations.missionIntro: Part 1: tap the five steps in the order they happen. Part 2: judge two live situations.
steps: FNOL. The client reports the loss. We register the claim and give them a claim number
Documents. Collect what is needed. For theft, the police report or FIR. For a crash, photos and the details of the other driver
Assessment. The surveyor checks the damage and confirms the loss is real and covered
Decision. Approve it, or decline it with the exact policy reason, explained to the client in writing
Payment. The approved amount reaches the client, and the claim is closed
stations.wrongFeedback: Not yet. Ask yourself one question. What must happen before this step can happen?

scenarios.text: A theft claim comes with NO police report, no FIR. The client is upset and wants payment today.

options.text: Pay now to make the client happy. Collect the FIR later
options.feedback: Kind, but no. The FIR is a must for theft claims. Without it, we cannot confirm the loss. Tell the client clearly what is needed, and help them get it. That is fast and correct.

options.text: Explain that the FIR is needed, and help the client arrange it
options.why: Exactly right. Honest about the rule, helpful about the process. The claim moves the moment the document arrives.

scenarios.text: A crash claim. The surveyor confirms accidental damage. It is fully covered and all documents are complete. Today is day 6 of 10.

options.text: Approve and pay. We are inside the promise
options.why: Right. The promise is a decision in 10 working days. A claim that is ready is decided when it is ready.

options.text: Hold it till day 10, to be more careful
options.feedback: Delay helps no one. Everything is checked. A ready claim should not make a worried client wait for money that is already theirs.

stations.success: Order right, judgement right. A claim done like this is why clients stay with us. Remember this. We do not pay fast or slow. We pay fair, and we explain everything.

stations.name: Systems Lab (CRM)
stations.objective: Follow the CRM journey of a policy. Lead, quote, issue, renewal.

intro.speaker: Hira
intro.text: Welcome to the Systems Lab. Everything Indus does with a policy lives in the CRM. If it is not in the CRM, it did not happen. The journey of a policy has five stages. Lead, Quote, Issue, Service, Renewal.

intro.speaker: Hira
intro.text: A new lead just came in. Walk it through the system with me. I will tell you what to do, and you will press the right button. The CRM has many buttons. Most of them are wrong for right now.

stations.missionIntro: Follow the instructions of Hira. One right action at every step. Watch the journey tracker fill up.

crmSteps.instruction: A website enquiry just arrived. Interested in family health cover.
crmSteps.action: Get her into the system as a new enquiry, so nothing about her is lost
crmSteps.coach: The enquiry of a stranger is a Lead. Nothing exists yet to issue or renew. Every journey starts at the start.

crmSteps.instruction: You spoke with her and noted the needs of her family. Now she asks: what will it cost?
crmSteps.action: Work out what her family's cover will cost, so she can decide
crmSteps.coach: She asked for the price. That is a Quote. Closing her as lost while she is asking to buy would be a strange achievement.

crmSteps.instruction: She accepted the quote, paid the first premium, and KYC is verified.
crmSteps.action: Make her cover official and active
crmSteps.coach: Paid and verified means issue the policy. The quote has done its job, and renewal is one year away.

crmSteps.instruction: Two months later, she calls. She has moved house and needs her address updated.
crmSteps.action: Update her record with her new address
crmSteps.coach: An old client with a change means a Service request on her record. Her policy does not change. Her details change.

crmSteps.instruction: Month 11. The renewal date of her policy is near.
crmSteps.action: Reach her in good time, so she can renew before the cover runs out
crmSteps.coach: Renewal time. A polite notice now, with a line about her claim free year, is how a policy lives to year two.

stations.success: Lead to renewal, with a clean record at every step. This trail helps any advisor open any client file and know exactly where things stand.

stations.name: Client Meeting Room
stations.objective: Run a full client meeting, from needs to issued policy.

intro.speaker: Mr. Sheikh
intro.text: Thank you for meeting us. We are the Sheikh family. Our first grandchild is on the way, so our son told us to sort out our insurance. Honestly, we do not know where to start.

intro.speaker: Mrs. Sheikh
intro.text: We only want our family safe if something happens to one of us. And we do not want anyone to sell us something we do not understand.

stations.missionIntro: Five moments will decide this meeting. Pick the answer an Indus advisor would be proud of.

beats.line: Mr. Sheikh: So, where do we begin?

options.text: Tell me about your family and what worries you most. Then we will look at the options together.
options.praise: Mrs. Sheikh smiles. Nobody has ever asked us that first.

options.text: Let me show you our most popular policy. Most families take it.
options.feedback: Products before needs is selling, not advising. We always start with their life, not our list of products.

options.text: First, sign this application, so we do not waste time.
options.feedback: Papers before understanding? Never. Nothing is signed until they know what they are choosing, and why.

beats.line: Mrs. Sheikh: Our income is mostly the job of my husband. If something happens to him…

options.text: Whole life is our premium product. Let us start there.
options.feedback: Premium for whom? Their need is maximum income protection on a family budget. That is the job of term life. Other products can fit later goals, not this first need.

options.text: Then the honest first step is to protect that income. Term life gives the biggest cover for the lowest premium while the children are young.
options.praise: Mr. Sheikh nods slowly. That actually makes sense.

options.text: Do not worry about such things. Think positive.
options.feedback: Kind words do not protect a family. Accept the worry. This worry is exactly why insurance exists.

beats.line: Mr. Sheikh: The premium is more than I expected. Is it worth it?

options.text: Everyone says that at first. You will get used to it.
options.feedback: Pushing a real worry away loses trust, and it loses the client. Answer the question he asked. Is it worth it? Show him.

options.text: I can quietly remove some cover to make it cheaper. No need to mention it.
options.feedback: Never quietly. A change in cover is a change in protection. Every change is explained, agreed and written down, or it does not happen.

options.text: Let us compare it with what it protects. Your family home and income for 20 years, for about the cost of one family dinner out, every month.
options.praise: Mrs. Sheikh: Put that way, it is the dinner we can skip.

beats.line: Mrs. Sheikh: My cousin said her policy gives good returns, guaranteed. Does yours?

options.feedback: That is the one promise an Indus advisor never makes. It is also not true. This is exactly how selling scandals begin.

options.text: No. And I will tell you this clearly, right now. This policy gives sure protection. Any growth in savings is a projection, never a promise. Anyone who promises returns is not honest with you.
options.praise: Mr. Sheikh leans back. Honest. That is rare. Please go on.

options.text: Let us not talk about returns today.
options.feedback: Avoiding a question is not honesty. She asked a straight question, and she deserves a true answer, in simple words.

beats.line: Mr. Sheikh: We are happy. What happens now?

options.text: Just sign here, here and here. I will fill the rest later.
options.feedback: Fill later is where disputes are born. Every field is completed together, and read before signing. That is the Indus way.

options.text: Payment first. Papers whenever we get time.
options.feedback: The order matters. Honest application, checked identity, then payment. Papers done whenever become papers never done.

options.text: We complete the application together. I check your CNICs for KYC. You read everything before you sign. And I will call you myself when the policy is issued.
options.praise: Both of them sign. Informed, unhurried, and smiling.

stations.success: Then it is settled. This is the first policy of our family. You explained everything, you promised nothing you could not keep, and we understand what we signed. This is why we will tell our friends about Indus.
